newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan market rises on select blue-chip demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordan market rises on select blue-chip demand.

text.p: Jordan's stock market rose on Tuesday with healthy institutional and floor trade demand on well-performing stock with a positive 1997 earnings outlook, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.74 percent to 153.57 points, its highest level this year in healthy 2,405,133 dinar ($3.4 million) turnover.

Trading was brisk despite two large blocs in Jordan Hotel and Tourism which owns Jordan's Intercontinental five star hotel and Industrial Development Bank which accounted for nearly half of daily volume.

"There was an improvement in prices regardless of the large bloc sales with some institutional buying and floor trader activity on stock with a good 1996 performance and that are expected to perform well in 1997," said Ibrahim Odeh, broker at Al-Wataniyah for Financial Services.

A five dinar rise in market heavyweight Arab Bank to 260 dinars helped underpin the official index. The share rose on expectations of a bonus share after the government approves soon a new companies law that abolishes a capitalisation tax.
The market is currently buttressed by brighter performance of industrials that stand to benefit from exports to Iraq, which helped give the market a good New Year kick-off on Saturday.

Some short-term investor focus is on drug, vegetable oils and detergent firms which have won export orders under Iraq's U.N. approved "oil-for food" deal, with hopes of improved half-year 1997 results.

Unified Transport Company, one of the companies that are seen benefiting from expanded transport activity with Iraq, rose 0.06 dinars to 2.21 dinars, with 199,023 dinars' worth of shares exchanging hands.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange rose 0.28 percent to 82.87 points from 82.63 points.
Rising shares outnumbered gainers on Monday by 25 to 10, with shares in five other firms trading but closing unchanged.
